publicComments.name: Chris R.
publicComments.summary: Raised legal concerns about using Prop 39 bond money for workforce housing under Article 13 of the California Constitution, questioned whether teachers actually want district housing, and suggested alternative funding mechanisms such as a parcel tax or housing vouchers.

publicComments.name: Elizabeth Starks
publicComments.summary: A multilingual Redwood City resident and former ESL teacher who expressed support for retaining good teachers but emphasized the greater need for after-school spaces and resources for children left unsupervised in the community.

publicComments.name: Maria Stockton
publicComments.summary: As leader of the classified union chapter, she defended the equal importance of classified staff, shared her own experience of rent increases outpacing raises, and expressed strong support for workforce housing to help staff who commute long distances remain in the community.

publicComments.name: Lupe Guzmán
publicComments.summary: The principal of Hoover Community School expressed strong support for workforce housing, noting that staff who live in the community strengthen it and that housing stress causes new teachers to leave the district.

publicComments.name: Mary
publicComments.summary: A visiting San Francisco school board member asked about the quality and durability of the construction and how the rental revenues flow relative to the bond repayment.

publicComments.name: Janet Cochise
publicComments.summary: A parent in the district since 2008 described how school closures and teacher departures due to unaffordable housing have repeatedly disrupted her child's education, and raised concerns about inadequate student transportation.

publicComments.name: Erin Washburn
publicComments.summary: President of the Redwood City Teachers Association confirmed that teachers do want workforce housing, sharing examples of colleagues whose lives improved with affordable housing and expressing support for the plan as a way to recruit and retain quality teachers.

items.title: School/Community Reports – Recommended Options to the School Board Regarding North Star Academy (NSA)

publicComments.name: Matt Schwal
publicComments.summary: Argued the NSA Forward Committee was negatively framed and called on board members to reframe the discussion positively and inspire change rather than break what is working.

publicComments.name: Cameron Hoffman
publicComments.summary: Argued the proposals are rushed and lack an evidence-based approach, and proposed a 'SHINE' talent development program modeled on the U46 district's AIM program to serve all neighborhood school students rather than restructuring North Star.

publicComments.name: Tony Webel
publicComments.summary: Shared his experience as both a Roosevelt and North Star parent, argued there is no data justifying grade configuration or location changes, and cited board bylaws requiring decisions be based on student learning and achievement.

publicComments.name: Diana Fu
publicComments.summary: Drew on her experience helping start the MI program to argue the district should provide more and better school choices rather than taking away the North Star option from parents.

publicComments.name: Lone Hin
publicComments.summary: Described her son's unmet needs at his neighborhood school and argued that dismantling or scaling back North Star would not serve any children in the district.

publicComments.name: Megan O'Neill
publicComments.summary: Argued that options A through C would eliminate half of North Star and fail to meet the stated goal of serving more students more effectively, and that no changes should happen until neighborhood schools can serve the needs of academically challenged students.

publicComments.name: Matt Collier
publicComments.summary: Urged the board to choose an option that allows K–8 programming to continue as a standalone school, sharing his personal experience benefiting from similar magnet programs.

publicComments.name: Anthony Low
publicComments.summary: As a Roy Cloud and North Star parent, argued all four options are deficient, that three of them effectively close 50% of North Star, and that his family would likely have to leave the district if a 6–8 option were chosen.

publicComments.name: Andrew Hoffman
publicComments.summary: Argued the board should focus on lifting lower-performing parts of the district rather than negatively impacting the award-winning North Star, and urged the board not to hastily approve incomplete recommendations.

publicComments.name: Heidi Wall
publicComments.summary: Argued the district should focus on systemic problems rather than dismantling a successful school, and cited the U46 model as a proven approach to improving diversity without restructuring.

publicComments.name: Susan Bouchard
publicComments.summary: Opposed the quota cap on neighborhood school transfers to NSA, arguing it would increase perceptions of elitism and division, and asked why the cap is not applied to all school-of-choice programs.

publicComments.name: Costas Dimitropoulos
publicComments.summary: Called for empirical evidence and proven models to justify any changes to North Star, noting that demographic differences between schools reflect local demographics rather than the influence of North Star.

publicComments.name: Kelly McCarthy
publicComments.summary: Questioned why the district is prioritizing North Star changes when so many students are underperforming post-COVID, and urged the board to use those resources to bolster neighborhood school programs instead.

publicComments.name: Casey Wright
publicComments.summary: Called the four options deeply flawed and irresponsible without fuller analysis of consequences, urged the board to postpone consideration and demand new options like those proposed by Cameron Hoffman.

publicComments.name: Catherine Stewart
publicComments.summary: Noted that all speakers before her opposed changes to North Star, and argued that the 'rising tide lifts all boats' principle means the school should be kept as-is rather than changed to reduce resentment from other schools.

publicComments.name: Gautam Dutta
publicComments.summary: As a North Star parent and community leader, echoed the sentiment that North Star is working well for his daughter and urged the board to reject all four options and instead focus on improving access and resources for all schools.

publicComments.name: Jing Su
publicComments.summary: Warned that the proposed changes would create many unhappy parents who would become reliable voters opposing the board, and urged trustees to consider the daily disruption to North Star families before making their decision.

publicComments.name: Kirsten McMullen
publicComments.summary: Argued the recommendations lack an evidence-based approach, only adequately solve the third-grade attrition problem while creating new unknowns, and urged additional research before selecting any option.

publicComments.name: Bara Altaba
publicComments.summary: As a parent of current NSA students who came from private school because of NSA, urged the board not to break a nationally recognized school and instead look at how to bring other schools up to NSA's level.

publicComments.name: Michelle Fogarty
publicComments.summary: Argued the proposals take direct aim at one successful school rather than addressing full district needs, and urged the board to take more time, examine the data framework, and conduct a new community survey before acting.

publicComments.name: Katie Goetz
publicComments.summary: As a North Star Forward Committee member, encouraged the board to move forward with the 6–8 Bayside option as the one proposal that addresses all three charges given to the committee.

publicComments.name: Christopher Bouchard
publicComments.summary: Urged the board to reject all four proposals and pause major changes, arguing the NSA Forward process was flawed from the beginning due to outdated and biased data, and called for a new community pulse survey.

publicComments.name: David Wright
publicComments.summary: Implored the board to defer the decision and request revised options informed by data that directly align to the committee's stated goals, rather than committing to deeply flawed options.

publicComments.name: Mike Beebe
publicComments.summary: Identified three broadly supported elements from Dr. Baker's plans (publicizing NSA, test prep/logistics help, and transportation), suggested spreading entrance grades across 3rd–5th to blunt the third-grade attrition pinch, and argued the board's primary focus should be the 52–72% of district students not at grade level.

publicComments.name: Meredith Park
publicComments.summary: As a Sequoia High parent and safe-routes advocate, warned that adding K–2 at the Duane location would worsen traffic, and suggested considering a neighborhood boundary middle school with an IB program at that site instead.

publicComments.name: Nathan Schmidt
publicComments.summary: Used a boat analogy to argue the board must focus on lifting underperforming schools rather than 'dumping water' into the one that is floating, urging them not to take action merely to appear as change agents.

publicComments.name: Mohamed Tabrizi
publicComments.summary: Ceded his time to Cameron Hoffman, agreed with her sentiments, and called the entire process a waste of resources that should have gone toward educating lower-income students, urging trustees to reject all options.

publicComments.name: Lily Melton
publicComments.summary: As an Orion parent, urged the board to move forward with bold structural changes, noting that a large community of district parents supports significant changes even if they are not the loudest voices tonight.

publicComments.name: Beatrice Chan
publicComments.summary: As a North Star parent, asked the board to present new options focused on introducing enrichment programs at community schools and helping current students meet grade-level expectations, rather than dismantling a successful model.

publicComments.name: Maribel Ng
publicComments.summary: Shared her daughter's struggles before finding North Star and argued that spreading the North Star philosophy of seeing students as individuals and loving what you teach across all Redwood City schools would fix many district-wide problems.

publicComments.name: David Weekley
publicComments.summary: Urged the board to keep students at the center of this process, ensuring North Star changes if it harms any students and that the focus remains on maximizing the potential of every student in the district.

publicComments.name: Lily Milton
publicComments.summary: Speaking as a North Star Forward Committee member and Orion parent, she expressed appreciation for the process and presented the subcommittee's key recommendations: changing grade configuration so North Star no longer begins at third grade, and bringing compacted curriculum and enrichment to all schools, while urging the board to act with urgency on broader equity issues.

publicComments.name: Unidentified speaker
publicComments.summary: Argued that the Bayside access data is misleading since many Bayside families already access North Star via school of choice, that North Star is not broken and serves its community at no extra cost, and urged the board to focus on the 70% of students who are academically behind rather than restructuring a well-designed school.

publicComments.name: John Kinsel
publicComments.summary: Expressed strong support for North Star as a program that keeps academically advanced students engaged and challenged, and suggested the real focus should be on improving conditions at other schools rather than changing North Star.

publicComments.name: Owen Webel
publicComments.summary: As a North Star graduate, shared that his previous school left him disengaged due to lack of challenge, while North Star allowed him to make friends at his own level and progress further academically.

publicComments.name: Tony Webel
publicComments.summary: As a North Star committee member and parent of children at both Roosevelt and North Star, he emphasized that the primary objective should be the best equitable learning environment for all students, and raised concerns that some committee ideas conflict with that goal, also requesting the Jamboard document be removed from materials as rushed and misleading.

publicComments.name: Jessica Nodi
publicComments.summary: As a Roy Cloud parent and educator, expressed support for starting North Star at kindergarten, bringing the enrichment model to all students at all sites, and offering equal enrollment percentages from all schools.

publicComments.name: Katie Morello
publicComments.summary: As a Henry Ford parent, described the emotional impact on her daughter losing 15 classmates and suggested that if North Star is a strong accelerated school, middle school might be a more appropriate entry point.

publicComments.name: Kaylee Vega
publicComments.summary: As a Henry Ford parent who chose the district partly because of North Star, argued that North Star is not the problem and that the other district schools being under-resourced and underperforming is the real issue, urging the board not to dismantle a highly ranked program.

publicComments.name: Loan Hin
publicComments.summary: As a Henry Ford parent who personally benefited from a magnet school as a child, stated her family would leave the district if North Star is not available at third grade, and argued that equity and access issues can be addressed without eliminating the North Star format.

publicComments.name: Elle Kolekar
publicComments.summary: As a Bayside family with children attending Hillside schools including North Star, argued that the equity problem is a deeper district-wide issue not caused solely by North Star, and called on the board to invest in and strengthen Bayside community schools.

publicComments.name: Alice Harkey
publicComments.summary: As North Star's parent club president, described the transformational impact of North Star on her children, expressed support for universal testing and expanded outreach including busing and after-school support for Bayside students, and asked the board to preserve North Star's curriculum and enrichment opportunities.

publicComments.name: Shonda Stewart
publicComments.summary: As a parent with children at both North Star and Orion, argued that North Star's parent fundraising perpetuates educational inequality, that the school culture is not socioeconomically inclusive, and that outreach to Bayside schools has been inadequate compared to Mandarin immersion community outreach.

publicComments.name: Katie Goetz
publicComments.summary: As a North Star Forward Committee member focused on third grade attrition, argued that enriched programming should be available to all RCSD students regardless of testing, since no student is more in need of enrichment than any other, and urged the board to pursue equity and justice for all students.

publicComments.name: Nicole Kowaki
publicComments.summary: Reading a condensed letter co-signed by 20 district parents, cited stark demographic disparities between North Star and the broader district to argue that North Star as currently constituted amounts to publicly funded education for the affluent, and urged the board to support the equitable solutions proposed by the North Star Forward Committee.

publicComments.name: Daryl Norcott
publicComments.summary: As a Clifford parent, argued that North Star inherently widens the achievement gap, that standardized testing is racially biased, that children who don't get in feel stigmatized, and that the enrichment model should be brought to students at their neighborhood schools rather than concentrating resources at one location.

publicComments.name: Heidi von Brielle

items.title: Second Reading and Approval of Board Policy 5116.1 - Intradistrict Open Enrollment

publicComments.name: David Weekley
publicComments.summary: Opposed the proposed transfer restriction, arguing it harms students and the district by reducing choice and will ultimately hurt enrollment in programs like Mandarin Immersion.

publicComments.name: Eric Liu
publicComments.summary: Opposed the policy as a Chinese-American parent of a Mandarin Immersion student, saying the proposal felt discriminatory by barring MI families from competing for North Star.

publicComments.name: Connie Kwan
publicComments.summary: Raised the unintended consequence that parents might be forced to pull their child from MI and place them in private school for a year just to preserve the option to apply to North Star.

publicComments.name: Peter Kwan
publicComments.summary: Raised concerns about timing, the fundamental problem of attrition rather than the symptom, and the lack of transparency around 'unspoken rules' in choice program enrollment.

publicComments.name: Dennis Lee
publicComments.summary: As a parent of a rising kindergartner newly accepted to MI, he opposed the policy for forcing families to predict years ahead what is best for their child and for penalizing choice-school families while potentially benefiting private school families.

publicComments.name: Michelle Hsu
publicComments.summary: Argued the root issue is that North Star and Mandarin Immersion are not set up on fair ground due to North Star's third-grade start and admissions process, and urged the committee to address equity in North Star admissions.

publicComments.name: Jennifer Barnett
publicComments.summary: Called the policy shortsighted and harmful to enrollment, arguing it will increase inequity, may turn North Star into a publicly funded private school, and urged addressing North Star's own issues instead.

publicComments.name: Diana Chang
publicComments.summary: Submitted written comment opposing the restriction as unnecessarily limiting for families who discover their first choice school is not the right fit, and asked the board to find more rational ways to achieve their objectives.

publicComments.name: Alvin Cheon
publicComments.summary: As an Orion parent participation parent, expressed concern that removing the North Star incentive would push committed families out of RCSD, and suggested alternatives such as distributing North Star-style culture across schools rather than concentrating it at one site.

publicComments.name: Christina Jade Lee Simmons
publicComments.summary: Urged the district to address structural inequality perpetuated by the North Star model, suggested starting North Star at sixth grade, and called for more enrichment across all elementary schools.

publicComments.name: Kyle Zeibes
publicComments.summary: Thanked the board for postponing the policy, argued it would harm equity and push families to private school, and suggested delaying North Star to sixth grade as a cleaner solution.

publicComments.name: Brian Hicks
publicComments.summary: Argued the proposed policy is the opposite of any long-standing unwritten rule, urged addressing the real problem rather than restricting choice, and requested that any new policy not apply retroactively to families already enrolled.

publicComments.name: Elle Kolekar
publicComments.summary: As an Orion parent participation parent with a child starting there in the fall, warned that the policy would drive families to private school and could effectively end the parent participation program.

publicComments.name: Keith Simmons
publicComments.summary: Echoed earlier concerns and highlighted that the superintendent-exception carve-out could create racial inequities because language and cultural barriers make it harder for immigrant families to petition for exceptions.

publicComments.name: Ting Cheng Wang
publicComments.summary: Opposed the policy because it effectively forces parents of kindergartners to choose their child's middle school years in advance, which is unfair.

publicComments.name: Megan O'Reilly Green
publicComments.summary: As Orion PTO co-president, argued that the fundamental problem is North Star's structure and its perceived status as the 'best' school, and that the policy would not ultimately harm MI recruitment since committed immersion families exist and the program has a waitlist.

publicComments.name: Elizabeth Flavel
publicComments.summary: Shared her experience choosing Adelante partly because she knew she could leave if it didn't work out, and cautioned that the policy may have unintended consequences for incoming families' enrollment decisions.

Discussion on COVID-19/Distance Learning

publicComments.name: Maureen McPeek
publicComments.summary: A Roosevelt second-grade teacher urged the board to wait until January 2021 to reopen, citing inadequate safety preparations, temperature-checking issues, lack of PPE, and concerns that behavior management would crowd out academic instruction.

publicComments.name: Jackie Moore
publicComments.summary: A Hoover special day class teacher argued for continuing full distance learning, citing COVID prevention, positive distance-learning outcomes for her SDC students, and personal financial inability to take unpaid leave.

publicComments.name: Nusheen Kavyani
publicComments.summary: A parent stated that current reopening plans carry the risks of COVID without the benefits of in-person learning, and urged that chat be open for public viewing to better simulate a public meeting.

publicComments.name: Mercedes Kwiatkowski
publicComments.summary: A child psychiatrist described alarming mental health trends among students during distance learning and proposed a pilot program using willing teachers and families as a first step toward cautious reopening.

publicComments.name: Sarah Henderson Martinez
publicComments.summary: A preschool teacher expressed concern about inadequate contact tracing, risk to elderly family members, children's inability to wear masks, a classroom move mid-year, and urged caution before reopening.

publicComments.name: Kathryn Stewart
publicComments.summary: A parent argued that teachers' lives are valuable enough for parents to tolerate the inconvenience of distance learning until it is truly safe for teachers to return, and pushed back on prioritizing children's social-emotional comfort over teacher safety.

publicComments.name: Eric Sutton
publicComments.summary: An Orion parent reported that 65% of first-grade Orion families preferred distance learning and 100% wanted to keep their current teachers, warned that the district's proposal would destroy the school's effective two-teacher distance model, and disputed blaming mental illness on distance learning.

publicComments.name: Christy Herrera
publicComments.summary: A kindergarten teacher argued the district should not reopen until the county reaches the yellow tier, said five-year-olds cannot developmentally comply with masking and distancing requirements, and described severe stress and health impacts on teachers caused by reopening pressure.

publicComments.name: Indra Hernandez
publicComments.summary: A preschool teacher said distance learning is working, urged the board to ensure preschool receives the same safety protocols as the rest of the district, and asked that safety come first so staff can continue to serve children.

publicComments.name: Ramin Kaivan
publicComments.summary: A business owner and husband of a preschool teacher argued that distance learning is working in his home, disputed mental health statistics, and warned that returning young children who cannot comply with PPE requirements would be dangerous.

publicComments.name: Laura Atherton
publicComments.summary: A special day class preschool teacher explained that her students cannot wear masks, require diaper changes and hand-over-hand feeding, and that physical distancing is impossible with young children with special needs, urging the board not to reopen preschool SDC.

publicComments.name: Mohammad Tabrizi
publicComments.summary: A parent urged the board to compare RCSD's reopening plan with Menlo Park City School District's more thorough plan, argued the district was ill-prepared to reopen safely, and called for rigorous safety and testing protocols as a prerequisite.

publicComments.name: Christina Kim
publicComments.summary: An Orion Mandarin Immersion parent reported that their community's own survey showed high flexibility and a strong desire to keep the MI program intact, and requested that the board support site-specific, collaborative solutions.

publicComments.name: Christina Hsu
publicComments.summary: An Orion Mandarin Immersion parent said the district survey caused confusion and anxiety in their community, and asked the board to allow individual sites and programs to work with their teachers and administrators on models that fit their specific needs.

publicComments.name: Devin/Michelle Mulaney
publicComments.summary: Speaker yielded their time without making substantive comments.

publicComments.name: Cameron Hoffman
publicComments.summary: A parent called for respectful, fact-based dialogue, asked teachers to articulate what they need to return safely, urged the board to speak up for the most vulnerable students, and noted that learning pods in his experience are working safely.

publicComments.name: Linda Elkins
publicComments.summary: A parent of three district students gave feedback that the survey's forced-choice format obscured nuances around teacher continuity, expressed support for a return to in-person learning in some form, and suggested leveraging parent expertise in planning.

publicComments.name: Melanie Haskell
publicComments.summary: A first-grade parent asked the board to continue offering independent study as an option regardless of the in-person decision, and recommended involving parents meaningfully in reopening committees as Menlo Park had done.

publicComments.name: Kerry Schmidt
publicComments.summary: A bilingual kindergarten teacher with 25 years in the district said she would love to be back in person but that returning without proper safety measures would not provide a safe learning environment and would distract from teaching.

publicComments.name: Kamli Nannini
publicComments.summary: A kindergarten parent and physician with an epidemiology background argued that teachers are essential workers, that actual COVID transmission risk from masked asymptomatic children is likely negligible, and that hearing from medical experts would increase teacher willingness to return.

publicComments.name: Megan O'Reilly Green
publicComments.summary: An Orion parent and PTO leader expressed frustration that the Orion program feels perpetually at risk, asked the board to stop characterizing Orion families as well-resourced, and urged genuine partnership and investment in program stability.

publicComments.name: Michelle Smith
publicComments.summary: An Adelante Selby parent expressed concern about the Spanish immersion program being at risk, noted that masks prevent teachers from modeling mouth movements for language learning, and raised worries about building ventilation and air quality.

publicComments.name: Michelle Butler
publicComments.summary: A teacher who uses a wheelchair said she loves her students and wants to return when safe, explained she is pursuing the interactive process but fears losing her job, and said managing COVID safety compliance would prevent effective reading instruction.

publicComments.name: Jeanette Serrano
publicComments.summary: A kindergarten teacher with 37 years of experience warned that class reconfiguration would restart the exhausting relationship-building process, said site-specific concerns should drive reopening decisions, and noted she cannot ensure families of her Latinx students are following the four pillars.

publicComments.name: Maria Stockton
publicComments.summary: A speaker suggested bringing back older students (grades 2–5) first rather than the youngest, since they can better manage masks and distancing, and asked the board to wait at least until the end of the first trimester before reopening any grade.

publicComments.name: Keely Vega
publicComments.summary: A kindergarten parent asked the board to respond to the suggestion of launching a willing-cohort pilot program and to explain how the district is learning from schools like Menlo Park that have already reopened.

publicComments.name: Whitney Glockner-Black
publicComments.summary: Raised concerns about students accessing inappropriate content on YouTube via school devices and urged the district to implement stronger content restrictions quickly.

publicComments.name: Katherine Stewart
publicComments.summary: Stated she does not want her child back in school until a vaccine is available, preferring the inconvenience of distance learning over the risk of death.

publicComments.name: Michelle Gagliardi
publicComments.summary: As a parent of a kindergartner in an SDC class, opposed returning to in-person learning because her son cannot wear a mask or social distance, and argued that students with disabilities face greater health risks.

publicComments.name: Mercedes Kwiatowski
publicComments.summary: As a psychiatrist in the community, expressed support for cautiously moving toward in-person learning given the mental health toll on children, while emphasizing teacher involvement in the planning process.

publicComments.name: Kristi Herrera
publicComments.summary: As a kindergarten teacher, strongly opposed returning to campus before the end of the first trimester, citing safety concerns about young children wearing masks, the disruption of existing teacher-student bonds, and the complications of shuffling staff and students.

publicComments.name: Sandy Hoover
publicComments.summary: As a TK/K teacher in a high-risk group, described the unavoidable close physical contact with young students involving bodily fluids, inadequate PPE, and the impossible choice between risking COVID infection or losing her income.

publicComments.name: Kerri Yen
publicComments.summary: As a parent of a kindergartner with an IEP for speech, supported returning younger students to in-person learning as soon as possible, noting that distance learning is driving inequity and that some families are already leaving RCSD for alternatives.

publicComments.name: Cameron Hoffman
publicComments.summary: As a parent of two district students, supported both teacher safety and in-person instruction for the most vulnerable learners, urging the district to learn from neighboring schools already reopening and to do everything possible for students with the greatest needs.

publicComments.name: Allison Oldford
publicComments.summary: As a parent of first graders currently in a safe childcare group setting, expressed support for a return to in-person instruction while also respecting teacher concerns, arguing the two positions are not at odds.

publicComments.name: Brian Crawford
publicComments.summary: As a parent of three district children, shared that his son's mental health has deteriorated significantly during distance learning and urged the board to continue working proactively with teachers to return to campus as soon as safely possible.

publicComments.name: Janelle Allen
publicComments.summary: As an immunocompromised parent of a kindergartner, opposed the plan to bring students back at the end of October and urged the board to wait until flu season is over, arguing online learning better preserves existing teacher-student bonds.

publicComments.name: Jennifer Wenzel
publicComments.summary: As an RCSD teacher of 13 years and mother of a toddler, opposed reopening given Redwood City's high COVID infection rate, children's higher viral load, and the risk of bringing the virus home to family members.

publicComments.name: Jeanette Serrano
publicComments.summary: As a 34-year kindergarten teacher, opposed returning TK-1 students to campus while the county is still in the 'substantial' red tier, citing the inability of young children to maintain masks or distancing and her own plans to seek a medical exemption.

publicComments.name: Sarah Latora
publicComments.summary: If returning to in-person, preferred Option 1 (AM/PM cohorts with cleaning between) over Option 2, raised concerns about funding for cleaning, and praised Clifford Elementary staff for their excellent distance learning.

publicComments.name: Susan Forquer
publicComments.summary: As a parent of first and second graders at Adelante Selby, strongly opposed moving students out of dual immersion programs during any return to school and urged a separate survey asking immersion families whether they would prefer to remain in distance learning to preserve language acquisition.

publicComments.name: Eric Sutton
publicComments.summary: As a parent of a first grader who is thriving in his current distance learning classroom, opposed disrupting existing student-teacher relationships mid-semester and expressed frustration at the prospect of students being reshuffled.

publicComments.name: Michelle Torito
publicComments.summary: Described the unsustainable workload teachers face with excessive planning, grading, emails, IEPs, attendance forms, and 10-12 hour days including weekends, and called for meaningful change.

publicComments.name: Christina Granado
publicComments.summary: Described her overwhelming workload as a third-grade teacher and asked whether existing data like newsletters and daily schedules could substitute for the new attendance forms.

publicComments.name: Vanessa Sanchez
publicComments.summary: Reported averaging 82.5 hours of work per week against a 32.5-hour contract and said the administration's suggestion that most tasks could be done in 6.5 hours on Wednesdays was a blatant disregard of teachers' reality.

publicComments.name: Rita Melton
publicComments.summary: Expressed that her workload is untenable and unsustainable, criticized the district's response letter to RCTA as lacking compassion and empathy, and asked why teachers are not treated with the same care they show students.

publicComments.name: Michelle Bond
publicComments.summary: Described working 12-hour days and weekends, detailed physical toll including cracked teeth and eye pain, and argued that every minute spent on clerical tasks like attendance is a minute taken away from quality instruction.

publicComments.name: Sharon Tsuchiyama
publicComments.summary: Described working 10+ hours a day seven days a week under a rigid five-and-a-half-hour live lesson schedule and asked for flexibility in schedules, small group structures, and office hours to better serve students.

publicComments.name: Megan Blackburn
publicComments.summary: Argued that current schedules are harmful to 10-year-olds and that planning 10 sets of synchronous and asynchronous lessons per subject in 6.5 hours while also grading, communicating with parents, and completing attendance is impossible.

publicComments.name: Monica Voltz
publicComments.summary: Spoke about working a minimum of 10-hour days seven days a week, the heavy personal and student impact of the schedule, and asked the board for support and a lighter workload so teachers can continue to do their jobs with heart.

publicComments.name: Heather Irani
publicComments.summary: A 31-year educator and 18-year RCSD teacher described spending Labor Day and another full day working at school with her daughter's help, learning colleagues across the district face the same massive workload that is simply not sustainable.

publicComments.name: Chelsea Williams
publicComments.summary: Described teaching three math curricula plus homeroom and enrichment, spending 8+ hours weekly on lesson creation alone, and working 30+ hours beyond contracted hours weekly, calling it unsustainable.

publicComments.name: Sandy Hoover
publicComments.summary: A TK teacher described 12-hour days five days a week, inability to sleep due to anxiety, and expressed uncertainty about how long she can continue at this pace.

publicComments.name: Christy Herrera
publicComments.summary: A kindergarten teacher of 20 years described minimum 12-hour daily workdays, severe eye strain, inability to find time for self-care, and urged the board to look into using existing platforms like Google Classroom and Seesaw to reduce the new attendance form burden.

publicComments.name: Stephanie Pappalardo
publicComments.summary: An RSP middle school teacher advocated for her special education students who are overwhelmed by multiple digital platforms and excessive screen time, and asked the board to rethink Wednesday requirements and reduce overall workload.

publicComments.name: Erin Washburn
publicComments.summary: As RCTA president, presented survey data showing 75% of members working more than 9 hours above contract and 43% working more than 16 hours above contract, called the situation a grievable contract violation, and outlined needed solutions including flexible schedules and streamlined attendance tracking.

publicComments.name: Angie Teeple
publicComments.summary: A 28-year fifth-grade veteran speaking at a board meeting for the first time described 12-hour days six to seven days a week, the burden of tech support and platform unfamiliarity, and asked the board to value teachers' well-being.

publicComments.name: Catherine Rivera
publicComments.summary: As principal of Orion Alternative School, acknowledged the difficulty of the year while offering a silver lining: the school's two parent communities have united in support of teachers and students, with parents recognizing and appreciating teachers' tremendous work.

publicComments.name: Mohammed Tabrizi
publicComments.summary: Criticized the district's decision to switch from Zoom to the inferior Google Meet platform last spring and the slow migration back to Zoom, arguing the delay caused unnecessary frustration and called on the board and district leadership to strive for and deliver excellence.

publicComments.name: Tia Knoedler
publicComments.summary: As a special education instructional assistant, supported teachers' concerns about the oppressive workload and urged the board to put teachers' needs first rather than letting parent demands drive the agenda.

publicComments.name: Marlena Goanna Mendoza
publicComments.summary: A special education teacher described going to a student's home on her prep day to teach him how to navigate his iPad, training her aides in technology, conducting home visits for IEP wet signatures, and completing overdue testing—all on top of an already impossible workload.

publicComments.name: Shannon Cody
publicComments.summary: Expressed love for the district and community while acknowledging the enormous challenges of distance learning, and called on the whole RCSD community—board, administration, staff, and families—to work together toward what is best for students.

items.title: Second Public Hearing: Neighborhood Schools Attendance Boundary Change Study

publicComments.name: Matt Collier
publicComments.summary: Requested that the board restore both sides of Alameda de las Pulgas to the Roy Cloud boundary in Scenario 3, as the change would split his children between two different schools.

publicComments.name: William Paxton
publicComments.summary: Expressed support for Scenario 3, particularly for keeping the Kentwood/Atherwood neighborhood assigned to Henry Ford School given the lack of pedestrian access to Garfield.

publicComments.name: Anna Fonseca Janoff
publicComments.summary: Asked whether the redistricting goal was to move away from neighborhood schools to larger comprehensive campuses, and questioned how Scenarios 1 and 3 would improve socioeconomic diversity at Roy Cloud compared to Scenario 2.

publicComments.name: Michael Bergeron
publicComments.summary: Representing the Woodside Hills HOA, requested that Woodside Hills be reassigned to Roy Cloud (K–8) to encourage families currently in private schools to return to public school and build community.

publicComments.name: Brian Varese
publicComments.summary: Leaned toward Scenario 2 as better for long-term balance and diversity, questioned whether the school-of-choice lottery is truly promoting diversity by design, and asked that whichever scenario is chosen address schools pushed to 80% or above capacity.

publicComments.name: Selena Holder
publicComments.summary: Supported Scenario 2, arguing that changing Roy Cloud's boundaries would encourage Selby Lane neighborhood families currently in private schools to return to public school and improve diversity.

publicComments.name: Keely Vega
publicComments.summary: Strongly supported Scenario 2 for long-term district balance, challenged the notion that school-of-choice seats promote intentional diversity, questioned the use of walkability as a boundary criterion, and asked how the board plans to weigh the survey showing 88% support for Scenario 2.

publicComments.name: Patricia Boers
publicComments.summary: Supported Scenario 2 to foster community among Woodside Hills children, noted her family's ethnic diversity and Spanish-speaking home as factors relevant to the diversity discussion, and pointed out that only about 30 students from Woodside Hills would be affected.

publicComments.name: Colleen Voss
publicComments.summary: Co-signer of the Selby Lane community letter supporting Scenario 2, argued it was unfair that the community-input Scenario 3 resembles Scenario 1 rather than the survey-preferred Scenario 2, and asked why Scenario 2 wasn't also refined with minor tweaks.

publicComments.name: Frank Hanig
publicComments.summary: Supported Scenario 2 or a minor tweak to Scenario 3 to include Woodside Hills in Roy Cloud, citing Fernside and Alameda as geographic barriers to Henry Ford and noting it would allow walkable K–8 attendance without significantly raising Roy Cloud's capacity percentage.

publicComments.name: David Eicher
publicComments.summary: Supported Scenario 2 to move Woodside Hills from Henry Ford/Kennedy to Roy Cloud, emphasizing the K–8 continuity that would help build community bonds and might bring private-school families back to public school.

publicComments.name: Lindsay Semple
publicComments.summary: Supported Scenario 2 or a Scenario 3 tweak assigning Woodside Hills to Roy Cloud, stating it would help build sub-community and move families away from private school or school-of-choice options.

publicComments.name: Abraham Fraley
publicComments.summary: Supported Scenario 2 for the Selby Lane area, citing dangerous crossing conditions on the state highway to Henry Ford, argued for boundary/demographic alignment with the Roy Cloud census area, and raised concerns about inherent bias when school-of-choice is prioritized over rezoned neighborhood students.

publicComments.name: Lisa Carr
publicComments.summary: Longtime Redwood City public school supporter living in Woodside Hills urged the board to listen to the strong community support for Scenario 2 or a Scenario 3 tweak including Woodside Hills in Roy Cloud, noting that neighborhood children are not currently attending public school.

publicComments.name: Katha Hall
publicComments.summary: Woodside Hills resident of 23 years supported having the neighborhood assigned to Roy Cloud to build community and bring children out of private schools, citing the 88% survey support for Scenario 2 as deserving respect.

publicComments.name: Kathryn Stewart
publicComments.summary: Asked for specific hours of live Mandarin-immersion instruction per day and cautioned against encouraging small-group playdates as a safety risk.

publicComments.name: Brian Cagle
publicComments.summary: Advocated for continuing PE instruction during distance learning and cautioned that outdoor learning would frequently be uncomfortably hot, cold, or wet.

publicComments.name: Christy Herrera
publicComments.summary: Asked for testing and contact-tracing protocols before return to campus, requested teachers be given the option to teach from home or classroom, and recommended waiting at least 14 days after holiday breaks before any in-person reopening.

publicComments.name: Michelle Torit
publicComments.summary: Supported the distance-learning decision and recommended postponing any school reopening until at least 14 days after winter break (January 19) to reduce exposure from holiday gatherings.

publicComments.name: Sandy Hoover
publicComments.summary: Stressed that timely testing, tracking, and tracing protocols must be in place before any return to campus, and expressed hope to meet her TK students in person this year.

publicComments.name: Jamie Guiena
publicComments.summary: Echoed support for keeping PE in the daily distance-learning curriculum to address students' physical, social, and mental health needs during sedentary remote schooling.

publicComments.name: Julia Feng
publicComments.summary: Thanked the board for including special-needs students in planning and asked what tools and strategies could help parents support very young learners who struggle or refuse to engage with screen-based learning.

publicComments.name: Kayla Kamley
publicComments.summary: As a first-grade teacher, urged the district to distribute technology and hotspots early, provide physical books and school supplies to students, and communicate class assignments and daily schedules to families well before the school year begins.

publicComments.name: Sarah La Torre
publicComments.summary: Proposed that the GATE program adopt a materials-pickup-plus-virtual-class model similar to the public library's art program to provide enrichment and a sense of normalcy during distance learning.

publicComments.name: Michelle Smith
publicComments.summary: Asked when child care options would be announced and which highest-need students would be prioritized, requested home supply kits for students, and urged that technology be distributed before the start of school to avoid loss of instructional time.

publicComments.name: Teresita Carlos
publicComments.summary: Thanked the board and staff, shared that she is keeping her own preschool child home to avoid exposure, praised a Henry Ford teacher for excellent distance-learning that combined online and paper-based activities, and supported waiting until after winter break to consider returning.

publicComments.name: Pam Barish
publicComments.summary: Kindergarten teacher of 30 years urged the board to pause reopening plans if pandemic conditions deem it unsafe.

publicComments.name: Laura Easley
publicComments.summary: Education reform professional and parent advocated for increased socio-emotional learning, planning for marginalized students, and collaboration with after-school providers.

publicComments.name: Mercedes Kwiakowski
publicComments.summary: Pediatrician and child psychiatrist recommended balanced metrics including mental health indicators, prioritizing K-2 in-person attendance, optimizing classroom instruction time, and a community commitment to minimizing exposures.

publicComments.name: Gloria Comfort
publicComments.summary: Asked unanswered questions about what happens when a teacher tests positive, including substitute coverage, student quarantine, testing costs, and notification protocols.

publicComments.name: Jeanette Melendez
publicComments.summary: Fifth grade teacher said she loves her job but is not comfortable returning in person given the spike in COVID cases and urged the board to choose full distance learning.

publicComments.name: Susan Forker
publicComments.summary: Thanked the board, asked when a decision would be made about starting in full distance learning even if the hybrid plan moves forward, and advocated for a more equity-focused approach to child care.

publicComments.name: Erin Washburn
publicComments.summary: Newly elected RCTA president and middle school music teacher cited unresolved safety questions and urged the board to choose full distance learning given rising case counts and county health stepping back from testing and tracing.

publicComments.name: Ariana Baltay
publicComments.summary: Eighth grade teacher of 20+ years opposed returning to classrooms, citing inadequate testing, restroom cleaning concerns, outdoor lunch needs, and incorrect application of stable cohort guidelines.

publicComments.name: Jennifer Overby
publicComments.summary: District teacher speaking as an essential worker advocate, calling for negative COVID tests before campus return similar to tuberculosis testing requirements.

publicComments.name: Caitlin McManus
publicComments.summary: Parent and middle school teacher said she cannot wait to return to in-person teaching but only if safe, and asked the board to consider full distance learning as other districts are doing.

publicComments.name: Michelle Packet
publicComments.summary: Teacher raised concerns about lack of hot running water, asymptomatic spread, inadequate PPE, inability to monitor distancing, special education support gaps, and noted COVID may be airborne with inadequate ventilation.

publicComments.name: Melanie Haskell
publicComments.summary: Parent asked for more specific information before choosing a learning model, particularly about positive case protocols, flexibility in distance learning schedules, an independent study option, and restoration of librarian services.

publicComments.name: Peggy Klein
publicComments.summary: Kennedy Middle School RSP teacher warned that COVID conditions do not yet meet Step 1 requirements, that many teachers may not return, and that distance learning with real teachers provides higher quality instruction than scrambling for substitutes.

publicComments.name: Candice Nance Kerrigan
publicComments.summary: Parent of incoming kindergartner asked about teacher training for remote learning and whether parents could serve as digital volunteers.

publicComments.name: Sandy Hoover
publicComments.summary: TK teacher at Clifford raised unanswered questions about illness tracking and school closure thresholds, and proposed starting with distance learning for one to two months to monitor case trends.

publicComments.name: Elle Kolekar
publicComments.summary: Parent sought clarity on whether distance learning students would still participate in school events, retain their school-of-choice placement, and receive daily instruction.

publicComments.name: Jennifer Mercado
publicComments.summary: Teacher said returning to in-person instruction is unsafe given rising cases and called for 100% distance learning until the rate falls below 100 per 100,000.

publicComments.name: Erin Washburn
publicComments.summary: In extended time ceded by colleagues, detailed unresolved practical safety questions and argued that full distance learning gives students more daily access to teachers and peers than the hybrid model, and that teachers have trained to do it well.

publicComments.name: Jocelyn Rutenberg Semke
publicComments.summary: Parent of incoming fifth grader opposed in-person learning due to rising cases and unknown long-term effects, and said distance learning would be more effective than a restrictive hybrid environment.

publicComments.name: Ann Lucero
publicComments.summary: Teacher argued that returning to school under current conditions would be a missed opportunity and compared the partial hybrid model unfavorably to doing distance learning well.

publicComments.name: Christina Kim
publicComments.summary: Parent of incoming Mandarin Immersion kindergartner said her family would choose full distance learning due to health-compromised family members, and asked for more detailed plans about what distance learning would look like for immersion programs.

publicComments.name: Dionne Smith
publicComments.summary: First grade teacher at Clifford recommended distance learning, citing fear of transmission in a classroom with new students, logistical and emotional challenges of safety protocols, and rising case counts in Redwood City.

publicComments.name: Ellen Jacobson
publicComments.summary: Parent and teacher thanked the board for following the data and urged redirecting planned safety investment toward technology and robust online learning.

publicComments.name: Tiffany Anderson
publicComments.summary: Henry Ford parent who witnessed COVID devastation firsthand urged the board not to knowingly risk teachers and staff whose science-based safety concerns deserve respect.

publicComments.name: Betsy Snow
publicComments.summary: Sequoia High School library media specialist supported distance learning and strongly opposed eliminating any library or librarian positions, arguing they are essential to literacy and can provide virtual services.

publicComments.name: Megan O'Reilly Green
publicComments.summary: Small business owner, licensed daycare provider, and PTO president proposed that PTOs help organize equitable child care solutions within educational cohorts during distance learning.

publicComments.name: Kathryn Stewart
publicComments.summary: Parent shared her experience running informal peer learning Zoom sessions and encouraged other parents to contribute similar support so teachers and families can share the load.

publicComments.name: Indra Hernandez
publicComments.summary: CDC preschool teacher thanked the board for their care, noted a current student is hospitalized with COVID, and urged continuation of distance learning until it is safe to return.

publicComments.name: Rita Melissa
publicComments.summary: Read a collective letter from 26 Adelante Selby teachers expressing belief that it is not safe to open schools and committing to a robust full distance learning model.

publicComments.name: Maribel Prado Parenti
publicComments.summary: Adelante Selby teacher clarified that teachers' calls for safety are about protecting the whole community—students, families, bus drivers, custodians, and all staff—not unwillingness to work.

publicComments.name: Eric Sutton
publicComments.summary: Roosevelt/Orion teacher used probability math to argue that social circles approach dangerous COVID exposure levels, and recommended smaller online groups and co-located student scheduling support.

publicComments.name: Katie Goetz
publicComments.summary: Parent of immersion students asked for clear guidelines on how non-native-speaking parents can support their children's immersion learning in a full distance model.

publicComments.name: Joan Perez
publicComments.summary: Sixteen-year district teacher expressed concern that teacher safety is not receiving enough attention, and noted that conditions for safe reopening—suppressing the virus—are not currently met.

publicComments.name: Julia Fang
publicComments.summary: Parent of young Mandarin Immersion students asked how immersion can be made interactive and engaging online for children who struggle to focus on screens, and requested as many instructional minutes as possible.

publicComments.name: Michelle Butler
publicComments.summary: Special education teacher and parent of an adult child with autism noted that some special ed students made meaningful progress on goals during spring distance learning and expressed confidence in improving the online model.

publicComments.name: Maria Stockton
publicComments.summary: CSEA president and 41-year district employee said she feels less assured about safe reopening as case numbers grow, and asked the district to meet with CSEA and RCTA to establish a process for notifying staff of on-site COVID exposures.

publicComments.name: Josefina
publicComments.summary: Fifth grade teacher and parent of a 10-year-old said keeping staff, students, and families safe is the priority, and urged the board to start fall with distance learning and revisit in spring based on data.

publicComments.name: Brian Howell
publicComments.summary: District teacher said he cannot protect students' physical safety in a classroom and argued that distance learning can reignite students' intrinsic joy of discovery.

publicComments.name: Jeanette Serrano
publicComments.summary: Kindergarten teacher in her 33rd and final year thanked the board for not asking teachers to sacrifice their safety on top of everything else they already give willingly.

publicComments.name: Franklin Herrera
publicComments.summary: Kennedy teacher and soccer coach said he misses students but asked whether the district wants to be part of the solution or part of the problem, arguing that reopening risks accelerating infections.

publicComments.name: Vanessa Sanchez
publicComments.summary: Second grade Adelante teacher urged distance learning to start the year, arguing the hybrid model wastes planning time and exposes communities with limited resources to disproportionate risk.

publicComments.name: Sarah Gurkes Suba Marty
publicComments.summary: Parent nursing a baby asked about flexibility in synchronous schedules for working parents and whether an independent study option modeled on Modesto City Schools could be offered alongside distance learning.

publicComments.name: Subha Mati
publicComments.summary: District technology coach in a high-risk health category said an early decision for distance learning would give teachers certainty and a relaxed mind needed to create optimal learning environments.

publicComments.name: David Weekley
publicComments.summary: Parent of incoming Mandarin Immersion kindergartner called for regular testing as a pillar of safe reopening and for more serious incorporation of outdoor instruction.

publicComments.name: Michelle Laird
publicComments.summary: Psychologist and special education preschool coordinator speaking for 30+ colleagues said their most vulnerable non-verbal students require hands-on teaching, and confirmed that one of their preschool students has tested positive for COVID.

publicComments.name: Joan Solari
publicComments.summary: Five-year district teacher said as much as teachers want to be back with kids, the science does not support in-person return and the board must follow the data.

publicComments.name: Jennifer Wenzel
publicComments.summary: Thirteen-year district teacher and mother of a toddler said sleepless nights worrying about bringing COVID home to her family reinforce her view that in-person opening would likely cause preventable deaths.

publicComments.name: Alex Herrera
publicComments.summary: Son of a 20-year district teacher and substitute teacher himself said returning to school would jeopardize thousands of people's health and stated he would not return as a sub.

publicComments.name: Michelle Mehrani
publicComments.summary: Twenty-year kindergarten teacher at Clifford said nothing makes her sadder than not greeting new kindergartners but that it is not safe for anyone on campus at this time.

publicComments.name: Sophie Minchin
publicComments.summary: Community member acknowledged the enormous burden on teachers under either model and urged the board to prioritize equity and additional child care solutions for families who cannot manage remote learning without support.

publicComments.name: Stephanie Kolsing
publicComments.summary: Orion teacher and superintendent's advisory council member said teachers fear for their safety and called for distance learning teachers to have safe access to classrooms, copiers, librarians, and custodians.

publicComments.name: Alec Duncan
publicComments.summary: Community member stated that without a vaccine, cure, or treatment, opening schools in August is not a good health choice and the potential consequences would weigh on everyone.

publicComments.name: Aida Ortiz De Aguilar
publicComments.summary: Preschool teacher asked the board to reconsider reopening the CDC separately from elementary schools and urged waiting to reopen preschool together with the rest of the district.

publicComments.name: Zoe Wilson
publicComments.summary: Eighth grade teacher said she feels distance learning is the right decision despite the heartbreak of not being face-to-face with students.

publicComments.name: Kayla Kamley
publicComments.summary: First-year teacher moving to first grade argued that starting online allows young students to build trust with teachers without the social-emotional harm of constant safety policing.

publicComments.name: Patricia Alcocer
publicComments.summary: Preschool teacher recommended continuing distance learning until the COVID curve declines and noted that preschoolers' natural sociability makes it very difficult to maintain distancing and mask protocols.

publicComments.name: Sylvia Antonelli
publicComments.summary: Adelante Selby third grade teacher said losing a human life is irreversible while the instructional model is reversible, and expressed full commitment to returning to the classroom when it is safe.

publicComments.name: Suzanne Ruiz Dunlap
publicComments.summary: District employee supported full distance learning and urged the board to continue conversations with special education preschool teachers about the unique challenges their students face.

publicComments.name: Jacqueline Rodriguez
publicComments.summary: Parent and community member (speaking partly in Spanish with chat translation) conveyed priorities from a community meeting with county officials: addressing learning loss, individualized supports, special population services, guaranteed instructional minutes, and child care and technology access.

publicComments.name: Patricia Perla
publicComments.summary: Preschool teacher recommended continuing distance learning until the COVID curve declines and until COVID testing is available as a prerequisite for reopening, noting families' fears about returning.

publicComments.name: Maria Elena
publicComments.summary: Special education teacher recounted seeing a COVID-positive adult removed from a family's apartment whose children attend the district, and called for everyone to be tested before being placed together at school.

publicComments.name: Mercedes Northern
publicComments.summary: Community member asked whether the board considered live scheduled daily classes with accountability as in private schools, outdoor classes for when school resumes, and counseling resources for at-risk students.

publicComments.name: Michelle Bond
publicComments.summary: Teacher noted that just as the district planned to pivot from hybrid to distance learning, the reverse is equally true—starting with distance learning allows a quick return to in-person when conditions allow.

publicComments.name: Elvira Cortez
publicComments.summary: Twenty-one-year district teacher and site supervisor at the Roosevelt CDC questioned why child development centers would be asked to open if it is unsafe for regular school, and urged the preschool not to open before the rest of the district.

publicComments.name: Gwen Minor
publicComments.summary: Community member cited CDC director's warning about the coming fall and winter being the most difficult in American public health history, and supported full distance learning while urging community collaboration on child care and trauma support.

publicComments.name: Adriana Behar
publicComments.summary: Preschool teacher and Garfield parent said it is too soon to reopen preschool next Tuesday and that teachers have trained for distance learning, with families supportive of continuing it.

publicComments.name: James Carrick
publicComments.summary: Teacher and parent said he did not enter teaching to gamble with lives, cited the death of a teacher who contracted COVID during summer school, and asked how many more must die before the district recognizes it is not the right time to reopen.

publicComments.name: Abed Kamal
publicComments.summary: Stanford instructor urged greater synchronous online teacher-student interaction based on his Zoom teaching experience, and recommended pool testing for staff and students as a condition for future in-person return.

publicComments.name: Michelle Ortez
publicComments.summary: Twenty-one-year Roy Cloud teacher and RCSD parent said this should not be parents versus teachers but parents and teachers versus COVID, and asked the community to redirect negative social media energy toward advocating for child care and teacher safety.

publicComments.name: Michelle Smith
publicComments.summary: Parent proposed using school sites as child care hubs for working and vulnerable families during full distance learning, and pointed to UC Berkeley's ATDP online program as a model of effective asynchronous and synchronous learning.

publicComments.name: Ariandi Jimenez
publicComments.summary: New Hoover third grade teacher said reopening would disproportionately harm communities of color, noting Latinx residents make up 49% of San Mateo County COVID cases while being less than 25% of the population.

publicComments.name: Linda Elkins
publicComments.summary: Parent of three elementary students and advocate for the hybrid model asked why both models could not be approved now so the district could pivot back to in-person as quickly as possible when conditions improve.

publicComments.name: Allie Gilmore
publicComments.summary: Parent of an incoming third grader and a special education preschooler said she is disappointed but hears the teachers, and asked the district to support parents as co-teachers, fill in distance learning details, and help parents advocate for needed county and state resources.

publicComments.name: Rob Hager
publicComments.summary: Parent of two fifth graders supported full distance learning, raised questions about teacher testing frequency, threshold metrics for switching models, temperature check protocols, and charter school compliance with district directives.

publicComments.name: Kathryn Stewart
publicComments.summary: Proposed a radical statewide lottery system for school assignment with pooled funding, eliminating the worst schools and modeling them after the best.

publicComments.name: Roberta Land
publicComments.summary: Expressed strong opposition to her Kentfield Commons neighborhood being assigned to Garfield, arguing it is not a neighborhood school and the route is dangerous for children.

publicComments.name: Katherine Hagman
publicComments.summary: Voiced strong support for Scenario 2, arguing it keeps the Mount Carmel neighborhood together and that the route to Clifford is safer for children than other options.

publicComments.name: Megan Maxwell Bay
publicComments.summary: Asked whether students currently attending a school of choice would be grandfathered in and allowed to remain at their existing school under boundary changes.

publicComments.name: Michelle Smith
publicComments.summary: Expressed concern about the lack of demographic data in the presentation, urging the board to consider equity and avoid de facto segregation when drawing boundaries.

publicComments.name: Meredith Park
publicComments.summary: Advocated strongly for walkable neighborhood schools and critiqued the school of choice model for fracturing neighborhood communities, noting her street's children attended 12 different schools despite all ending up together at Sequoia High.

publicComments.name: Cameron Matthews
publicComments.summary: Asked about population trend methodology behind the 2026 projections, requested walkability analysis tools for boundary fringe areas, and inquired whether additional scenario options beyond Scenarios 1 and 2 would be presented before the board vote.

publicComments.name: David Knox
publicComments.summary: Asked for clarification on whether students currently in the Roy Cloud boundary would be reassigned to another school under the proposed scenarios and whether grandfathering would apply.

publicComments.name: Eurydia Aquino
publicComments.summary: Asked whether her children, who attend RCSD schools via inter-district transfer while she works in the district, would be displaced or need to reapply under boundary changes.

publicComments.name: Annie and Andreas Hildebrandt
publicComments.summary: Expressed strong support for Scenario 2, sharing that their son moved from private school to Roy Cloud and found community, and that neighbors would also enroll in public school under that scenario.

publicComments.name: Stephen Gay

items.title: Discussion on the Safe Reopening of RCSD School Campuses this Fall of 2020-21

publicComments.name: Christy Herrera
publicComments.summary: A 19-year kindergarten teacher argued that the hybrid model is unworkable for kindergartners given COVID restrictions, and strongly recommended 100% distance learning for TK/K students to avoid trauma and allow proper acclimation.

publicComments.name: Sarah Latora
publicComments.summary: A parent of a third and fifth grader praised Clifford Elementary staff, raised concerns about mask-wearing barriers for children with vision/sensory issues, requested consistent scheduling for siblings, suggested grouping full-distance-learning students across sites with a single teacher, and supported team teaching.

publicComments.name: Sandy Hoover
publicComments.summary: A TK teacher at Clifford advocated for full distance learning as the best model to keep staff, students, and families safe while still delivering curriculum, and suggested it would allow children to acclimate positively before returning in person.

publicComments.name: Jacqueline Rodriguez
publicComments.summary: A parent leader proposed the creation of a parent committee to collaborate with the district on decisions about returning to school, and thanked board members who met with parents.

publicComments.name: Alexandra Sawiski
publicComments.summary: An essential worker and sole guardian expressed concern about lack of support for working parents during distance learning, and asked for help with the Spanish-language component of her child's Adelante immersion program.

publicComments.name: Maria Elena Arteaga
publicComments.summary: A parent leader echoed the request for a parent committee to be involved in back-to-school decision-making and thanked board members who attended parent meetings.

publicComments.name: Jenny Overby
publicComments.summary: A teacher thanked Dr. Baker and the board for the professional development week, praised frontline essential workers, and asked what the district's plan is for regular COVID testing of all staff before and during the school year.

publicComments.name: Abid Kama
publicComments.summary: A Stanford instructor asked whether there is data showing that live teacher instruction is more effective than packaged online modules, and also asked whether there is a plan to make up lost instructional hours and whether staff would be compensated for them.

publicComments.name: Michelle S.M.
publicComments.summary: A community member questioned why Fridays were chosen as the off/cleaning day rather than Wednesday, raised concerns about enforcing six-foot distancing with young children, supported the idea of district-wide distance-learning teachers for students not returning, and stressed the need for child care solutions for both families and teachers.

publicComments.name: Mercedes Northen and Rex Northen
publicComments.summary: Two parents speaking together asked the district to articulate clear educational goals for the new year — including restoring grading, increasing teacher-student interactivity, and improving Spanish immersion instruction — expressing concern that lowered expectations harm all students, especially those who were excelling or most disadvantaged.

publicComments.name: Rosemary Campos
publicComments.summary: A parent asked for more explanation of why a five-day AM/PM model is not feasible, raised concerns about immersion program quality in all three models, asked how decision-making committees were formed, and questioned how teachers with health concerns will be accommodated and whether cleaning staff capacity is sufficient.

publicComments.name: Jen Cook
publicComments.summary: A parent of an incoming kindergartner expressed serious doubt that any of the proposed models can effectively deliver Spanish immersion to a five-year-old in a home without native Spanish speakers, and asked for clear communication to incoming kinder families about how immersion challenges will be mitigated.

publicComments.name: Christopher Rosan
publicComments.summary: A parent echoed concerns about immersion fundamentals for kindergartners at Adelante/Selby, and suggested that unused open campuses in the district could be utilized to address space constraints for physical distancing.

publicComments.name: Michelle Buetler
publicComments.summary: A teacher expressed doubt that school can function normally under COVID restrictions, especially for primary and special-education students, and called for creative outside-the-box thinking such as one in-person day per week combined with flexible remote learning, and allowing medically vulnerable teachers to serve larger distance-learning caseloads.

publicComments.name: Ceri Phillips
publicComments.summary: A parent of a first grader and incoming kindergartner stressed that the learning loss is a long-term issue affecting the whole year, argued that kindergartners cannot effectively learn online with a teacher they have never met in person, and noted that even non-essential workers will eventually need to return to work and require child care support.

publicComments.name: Ali Gilmore
publicComments.summary: A parent of a child receiving IEP therapy services asked for more detail on plans for special education — both mainstream accommodations and therapy services — noting that remote learning has been largely inaccessible or ineffective for students with special needs and asking whether outside providers, IEP modifications, or different in-person models are being considered.

publicComments.name: Heather Morey
publicComments.summary: Speaking on behalf of PE Plus, she thanked the district for its partnership and the professional development time, and offered PE Plus's continued support in whatever form next year takes.

publicComments.name: Patricia Tez
publicComments.summary: Speaking on behalf of North Fair Oaks area parents, she asked about continuity of school lunch and dinner programs under distance learning, how teachers will detect child abuse when not seeing students in person, and how the district will support non-English-speaking, non-tech-savvy parents and students experiencing depression or housing/job instability.

publicComments.name: Victor Hernandez
publicComments.summary: Executive Director of PCC School Age Childcare offered PCC's support to the district in providing child care, noting they successfully supported distance learning during the last two weeks of school and are ready to expand capacity at their current or a new campus.

publicComments.name: Karina Perez
publicComments.summary: A Garfield parent of two children advocated for Option 1 (full distance learning), arguing that Option 2 is unworkable given parent refusals and that Option 3 places too heavy a burden on teachers, while praising her children's teachers for their communication and virtual classes.

publicComments.name: Daniel Hecht
publicComments.summary: A parent of an upcoming first grader at Adelante Selby expressed dissatisfaction with all proposed plans, raised the possibility of homeschooling or private school, and asked how many parents have expressed interest in leaving the district and how that affects enrollment and funding.

publicComments.name: Marlena Goanna
publicComments.summary: A special education paraeducator working with kinder–second grade students with significant needs described the physical impossibility of maintaining six-foot distance while caring for students who need diaper changes, hand-over-hand support, or have elopement behaviors, and reported remarkable student progress during distance learning, expressing worry about regression if students return under restrictive conditions.

publicComments.name: Carrie Schmidt
publicComments.summary: A 25-year bilingual teacher and reading specialist at Hoover acknowledged the trauma of the switch to distance learning, emphasized the importance of social-emotional wellbeing and parent partnership, expressed concern about children who depend on school as a safe haven, and said she personally favors a hybrid model but recognizes the virus ultimately dictates what is possible.

publicComments.name: Nora Aguirre
publicComments.summary: Did not speak — the board was unable to locate or unmute her; a board member noted that the Special Ed Director Dr. Palino would call her the following day regarding her special education questions raised at a prior meeting.
